About Mersenne’s Discovery:

In the 1630s, Marin Mersenne compared the instant flash from a cannon with the delayed boom. Knowing the distance and measuring the time helped him estimate how fast sound travels.

He also studied echoes. Because an echo travels to a wall and then back again, it covers twice the distance to the wall.

Cannon: v = d ÷ t    Echo: v = 2d ÷ t

v means speed, d means distance, and t means time.

Classroom model: This simulation uses 343 m/s, approximately the speed of sound in air near 20°C. Temperature and humidity can change the real speed slightly.
